lessons.title: Pearls! Pearls! Pearls!
lessons.learn_line: The long history of the pearl and why people in ancient times valued it so highly.
warmup: Have you ever seen a pearl? Where do pearls come from?
Why do you think people value pearls and other gems?
Which ancient civilisations have you heard of?
Why might a precious gem be a sign of wealth or status?

reading.summary_en: This lesson tells the long history of the pearl. The first pearl was probably discovered thousands of years ago while human beings were searching for food at the seashore, and throughout history the pearl, with its shine, has been one of the most highly valued gems. Pearls are mentioned many times in religious texts and mythologies from the earliest times. The ancient Egyptians valued pearls so much that they were buried with them, and it is said that the famous queen Cleopatra would dissolve a pearl in a glass and drink it as a sign of love and respect for the whole nation. The Greeks thought of pearls as a sign of wealth and social position, and associated their beauty with love and marriage. In ancient Rome, pearls were considered the greatest sign of wealth and social status; young women of noble families loved to wear beautiful pearl necklaces, and brave knights used to wear them in battles for good luck.
reading.gist_bn: এই পাঠে মুক্তার দীর্ঘ ইতিহাস বলা হয়েছে। হাজার বছর আগে সমুদ্রতীরে খাবার খুঁজতে গিয়ে প্রথম মুক্তা আবিষ্কৃত হয়; এর উজ্জ্বলতার জন্য এটি চিরকাল মূল্যবান রত্ন। ধর্মগ্রন্থ ও পুরাণে বহুবার মুক্তার উল্লেখ আছে। প্রাচীন মিশরীয়রা মুক্তাকে এত মূল্য দিত যে মৃতদেহের সঙ্গে কবর দিত; রানি ক্লিওপেট্রা নাকি গ্লাসে মুক্তা গলিয়ে পান করতেন। গ্রিকদের কাছে মুক্তা ছিল ধন ও সামাজিক মর্যাদার চিহ্ন, ভালোবাসা-বিয়ের সঙ্গে যুক্ত। প্রাচীন রোমে মুক্তা ছিল ধন-মর্যাদার সর্বোচ্চ চিহ্ন; অভিজাত নারীরা মুক্তার মালা পরত, আর সাহসী যোদ্ধারা যুদ্ধে সৌভাগ্যের জন্য পরত।

short_answers.q: Do you think pearls were discovered by accident? Why?
short_answers.model: Yes, pearls were probably discovered by accident. The first pearl was likely found thousands of years ago while human beings were searching for food at the seashore, not while looking for gems.

short_answers.q: Why do you think pearls were valued so much in the past?
short_answers.model: Pearls were valued for their natural shine and beauty, which made them one of the most precious gems. They became signs of wealth, social status, love and good fortune in many ancient cultures.

short_answers.q: How did the Greeks and Romans regard pearls?

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph on 'The Value of Pearls' (about 80 words).
writing.model: The pearl is one of the oldest and most admired gems in the world. Discovered thousands of years ago at the seashore, it has always been prized for its soft, natural shine. In ancient times, the pearl was far more than an ornament. The Egyptians were buried with pearls, the Greeks linked them with love and marriage, and the Romans saw them as the greatest sign of wealth and social status. Brave knights even wore pearls in battle for good luck. To this day, the delicate beauty of the pearl makes it a treasured gem.

lessons.title: The Ama Divers
lessons.learn_line: How pearls were once harvested by daring divers, and the famous Ama women divers of Japan.
warmup: Where did people get pearls before pearl farming began?
How long do you think a person can hold their breath underwater?
Why would diving deep into the sea be dangerous?
Would you like a job that is risky but full of skill? Why?

reading.summary_en: Before the beginning of the 20th century, pearls were obtained from pearl oysters collected from the bottom of the ocean, a lake or a river. To get enough pearl oysters, free-divers were often forced to descend more than 100 feet in one breath. Because diving was so difficult, pearls were of different quality and very rare. In Asia, some pearl oysters could be found on shoals at a depth of 5 to 7 feet, but at times divers had to go 40 feet or even up to 125 feet to find enough oysters, and these deep dives were extremely hazardous. In some fishing villages along the coast of Japan there are amazing women known as 'Ama divers'. The word 'Ama' means 'women of the sea'. They are independent divers who make their living by diving to depths of up to 25 metres without oxygen tanks or other breathing equipment. They rely on their own skills and breathing techniques to push down to the sea bottom and back, and can hold their breath for up to two minutes. Careful watching, lung capacity and hunter instincts are their special qualities. However, many young villagers now go to the city for other jobs, and the remaining Ama divers are aged between 50 and 60, with some still diving in their 70s. If young people do not take up Ama diving, this profession will soon die out.
reading.gist_bn: বিশ শতকের আগে সমুদ্র, হ্রদ বা নদীর তলদেশ থেকে মুক্তা-ঝিনুক সংগ্রহ করে মুক্তা পাওয়া যেত। যথেষ্ট ঝিনুক পেতে ডুবুরিদের এক নিঃশ্বাসে ১০০ ফুটের বেশি নামতে হতো; কঠিন বলে মুক্তা ছিল বিরল। এশিয়ায় কখনো ৫-৭ ফুট, কখনো ৪০-১২৫ ফুট নামতে হতো—অত্যন্ত বিপজ্জনক। জাপানের উপকূলে নারী ডুবুরিরা 'Ama' ('সমুদ্রের নারী') নামে পরিচিত; অক্সিজেন ট্যাঙ্ক ছাড়াই ২৫ মিটার পর্যন্ত নামে, দুই মিনিট পর্যন্ত শ্বাস ধরে রাখতে পারে। কিন্তু তরুণরা শহরে চলে যাওয়ায় অবশিষ্ট ডুবুরিরা ৫০-৬০ বছর বয়সী; পেশাটি বিলুপ্ত হওয়ার ঝুঁকিতে।

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph on 'A Risky Occupation' (about 100 words).
writing.model: Some occupations are full of danger, yet people do them with great skill and courage. The Ama divers of Japan are a fine example. These women make their living by diving up to twenty-five metres into the sea without any oxygen tanks, holding their breath for up to two minutes to gather oysters and other sea life. Their work demands careful watching, strong lungs and steady nerves, for a single deep dive can be hazardous. Sadly, as young people move to the cities for safer jobs, fewer take up this profession, and the remaining divers are growing old. Such brave and skilful occupations deserve our respect before they disappear.

lessons.title: River Gypsies in Bangladesh (1)
lessons.learn_line: Who the river gypsies (bedey) of Bangladesh are and how they live and earn on the water.
warmup: Have you ever seen people living on boats? What were they doing?
What does it mean to live a 'nomadic' life?
What jobs might people who live on rivers do?
Why might some people not have a permanent home on land?

reading.summary_en: River gypsies are an ethnic group of people in Bangladesh, known to local people as 'bedey'. They have their own lifestyle and culture, live in groups, and do not own any land, so they live a nomadic life, travelling from place to place. They roam across rivers and waters from May to December in small country boats, which are their houses, making them a part of our waters. In winter, when many water bodies dry up, they return to the mainland and live in make-shift tarpaulin tents on open river banks; there you can see their men relaxing, toddlers playing with pets in the dust, and women picking lice in rows. Throughout the monsoon they stay busy fishing and sometimes diving for natural pearls. Their men catch snakes, entertain people with snake charming and sell herbal cures, while their women go door to door selling bangles, cosmetics and other things, and also try to heal the pains of old people by sucking out blood. Many villagers believe in the gypsies' magical power and think they can make an evil spirit leave someone's body by magic or special powers.
reading.gist_bn: নদী-জিপসিরা বাংলাদেশের একটি নৃগোষ্ঠী, স্থানীয়ভাবে 'বেদে' নামে পরিচিত। তাদের নিজস্ব জীবনধারা ও সংস্কৃতি আছে; দলবদ্ধভাবে থাকে, কোনো জমির মালিক নয়, তাই যাযাবর জীবন কাটায়। মে থেকে ডিসেম্বর ছোট নৌকায় নদীতে ঘুরে বেড়ায়—নৌকাই তাদের ঘর। শীতে জলাশয় শুকিয়ে গেলে তীরে তারপুলিনের তাঁবুতে থাকে। বর্ষায় মাছ ধরে, কখনো মুক্তার খোঁজে ডুব দেয়। পুরুষরা সাপ ধরে, সাপের খেলা দেখায়, ভেষজ ওষুধ বিক্রি করে; নারীরা ঘরে ঘরে চুড়ি-প্রসাধনী বিক্রি করে, বয়স্কদের ব্যথা সারাতে রক্ত চুষে বের করে। অনেক গ্রামবাসী তাদের জাদুশক্তিতে বিশ্বাস করে।

summary.model: River gypsies, known locally as 'bedey', are an ethnic group in Bangladesh with their own culture. Owning no land, they live a nomadic life, roaming the rivers in small boats from May to December and using the boats as their homes. In winter they camp in make-shift tarpaulin tents on the river banks. The men fish, dive for pearls, catch snakes, do snake charming and sell herbal cures, while the women sell bangles and cosmetics door to door and heal the pains of old people. Many villagers believe the gypsies possess magical powers.

writing.prompt: Imagine you meet a bedey (river gypsy) woman. Write a dialogue asking her about her life and work.
writing.model:
You: Good afternoon. May I ask you a few questions about your life?
Bedey woman: Good afternoon. Yes, but please be quick; I am busy cooking.
You: Of course. How long have you been living in this camp?
Bedey woman: About four months. When the rains come, we will go back to the rivers.
You: What does your family do for a living?
Bedey woman: We catch fish, and our men are snake charmers. I sell bangles and cosmetics from house to house.
You: How do you treat sick people?
Bedey woman: We use traditional herbs and old healing methods to ease their pains.
You: Does your child go to school?
Bedey woman: Not yet, but I have heard of boat-schools on the river. I will try to send him to one.
You: Thank you for your time. I wish your family well.
Bedey woman: Thank you, too.

lessons.title: River Gypsies in Bangladesh (2)
lessons.learn_line: The problems river gypsies face today and how they are slowly joining mainstream life.
warmup: What problems might people who live on boats face today?

Why is education important for every child?

reading.summary_en: River gypsies in Bangladesh face various problems. First, Bangladesh is getting urbanised very rapidly, so the gypsy people are losing their customers among the urban population, and their income is threatened. Secondly, the 24,000 kilometres of waterways the country once had shrink to only 6,000 kilometres in dry seasons. Scientists believe Bangladesh will be worst affected by global climate change; unpredictable rain and the drying out of rivers have heavily restricted boat movement. Thirdly, in the context of this changed reality, many river gypsies are thinking of living permanently on land. The state feels that river gypsies need help to survive in the mainstream population, so the government is offering them voting rights, permanent housing and bank-loan facilities, although such changes do not come overnight. Traditionally, river gypsies are used to water life and have inherited the necessary life skills from their forefathers, but they have no education or training to adapt to modern society. As they have no permanent living place and their children are born and brought up on boats, they cannot go to conventional schools. Therefore, mobile boat-schools are being established, and some voluntary organisations are running special schools on boats to educate river gypsy children.
reading.gist_bn: নদী-জিপসিরা নানা সমস্যায় আছে। প্রথমত, দ্রুত নগরায়ণে শহুরে ক্রেতা হারিয়ে আয় হুমকিতে। দ্বিতীয়ত, দেশের ২৪,০০০ কিমি জলপথ শুষ্ক মৌসুমে কমে ৬,০০০ কিমি হয়; জলবায়ু পরিবর্তনে অনিয়মিত বৃষ্টি ও নদী শুকিয়ে নৌচলাচল ব্যাহত। তৃতীয়ত, অনেকে স্থায়ীভাবে ডাঙায় বসবাসের কথা ভাবছে। সরকার ভোটাধিকার, স্থায়ী বাসস্থান ও ব্যাংক-ঋণ দিচ্ছে। ঐতিহ্যগতভাবে তারা জলজীবনে অভ্যস্ত, পূর্বপুরুষ থেকে দক্ষতা পেয়েছে, কিন্তু আধুনিক সমাজের জন্য শিক্ষা নেই। নৌকায় জন্ম নেওয়া শিশুরা সাধারণ স্কুলে যেতে পারে না, তাই ভাসমান নৌকা-স্কুল চালু হচ্ছে।

writing.prompt: Imagine there is a boat-school in your area for river gypsy children. Write a short composition on how you can help the gypsy children with learning (about 150 words).
writing.model: If there were a boat-school for river gypsy children in my area, I would gladly do my part to help them learn. First, I would collect old books, exercise books, pens and pencils from my friends and neighbours and donate them to the school, since many gypsy families are too poor to buy these things. Secondly, on holidays I could visit the boat-school and help the younger children with their reading, writing and counting, making the lessons fun with songs and simple games. I would also teach them about cleanliness, good manners and the importance of education, so that they dream of a better future. Moreover, I would request my school and local people to support the boat-school with money and volunteers. River gypsies are an integral part of our country, and their children deserve the same chance to learn as we do. By helping them, we help build a kinder and more equal society.

lessons.title: Refugees (Sea Prayer)
lessons.author: Khaled Hosseini
lessons.learn_line: A father's heartfelt letter to his son as they flee war — a window into the lives of refugees.
warmup: Who are refugees, and why do people become refugees?
How do you think it feels to leave your home forever?
What might a parent feel while trying to protect a child in danger?
Why should we feel sympathy for people fleeing war?

reading.summary_en: This lesson presents 'Sea Prayer' by Khaled Hosseini, written as a father's tender letter to his young son, Marwan, on a cold, moonlit beach. The father remembers his own peaceful boyhood at his grandfather's farmhouse outside Homs, Syria, waking to olive trees stirring in the breeze and the sounds of farm life. He recalls the bustling Old City of Homs, with its mosque, church and grand souk where everyone would haggle, and the evening walks around Clock Tower Square. But that life now feels like a long-dissolved dream. First came the protests, then the siege, then bombs, starvation and burials, the only world his son has ever known. Now the father, his wife and son sit among other refugees, Afghans, Somalis, Iraqis, Eritreans and Syrians, all waiting in dread to cross the sea in search of home, feeling unwelcome and uninvited. As his son sleeps in guileless innocence, the father admits how powerless he is to protect him from the deep, vast, indifferent sea, so all he can do is pray that God will steer the vessel safely, because his son is the most precious cargo there ever was.
reading.gist_bn: এই পাঠে খালেদ হোসেইনির 'Sea Prayer'—এক বাবার তার ছোট ছেলে মারওয়ানকে লেখা কোমল চিঠি, এক শীতল জ্যোৎস্নাভরা সৈকতে। বাবা সিরিয়ার হোমসে নিজের শান্ত শৈশব স্মরণ করেন—দাদার খামারবাড়ি, জলপাই গাছ, প্রাণবন্ত পুরোনো শহর, মসজিদ-গির্জা-বাজার। কিন্তু এরপর এল বিক্ষোভ, অবরোধ, বোমা, অনাহার, মৃত্যু—এই-ই ছেলেটির চেনা পৃথিবী। এখন তারা অন্য শরণার্থীদের সঙ্গে সমুদ্র পাড়ি দেওয়ার অপেক্ষায়। ঘুমন্ত ছেলেকে সমুদ্রের বিপদ থেকে রক্ষা করতে অসহায় বাবা কেবল প্রার্থনা করতে পারেন—তার ছেলেই সবচেয়ে মূল্যবান।

writing.prompt: Write a paragraph on 'The Sufferings of Refugees' (about 100 words).
writing.model: Refugees are among the most unfortunate people in the world. They are forced to leave their homes because of war, violence or disaster, losing everything they once loved. As we see in 'Sea Prayer', a peaceful city can be destroyed by protests, siege and bombs, turning ordinary families into homeless wanderers. Refugees often travel long, dangerous distances, crossing rough seas in crowded boats with little food or safety. Many feel unwelcome in new lands, yet all they truly want is a safe home and a future for their children. We should treat refugees with kindness and sympathy, for they have suffered far more than most of us can imagine.
